resources.string: AutoSkip
Presses YouTube\'s own Skip button for you as soon as it appears. It never blocks ads.
AutoSkip for YouTube

Presses the Skip button in the YouTube app for you once YouTube shows it, and can mute ads while they play. It only looks at the YouTube app, never reads other apps, keeps nothing it sees, and has no internet access.
On
Watching the YouTube app. Play a video with an ad to try it.
Off
Turn on AutoSkip in Accessibility settings. Android doesn\'t let apps do this for themselves.
Turned on, but not running
Android has stopped the service. In Accessibility settings, turn AutoSkip off and on again, then check that battery saving isn\'t closing this app.

What it accesses: AutoSkip uses Android\'s Accessibility API to read the YouTube app\'s screen, so it can find the Skip button and press it. It reads nothing from other apps, stores nothing it sees, and cannot send data anywhere because it has no internet permission.
Open Accessibility settings
Accessibility settings
The YouTube app isn\'t installed on this phone. AutoSkip only works with the official YouTube app.
Switch greyed out, or a \"Restricted setting\" message?

Android 13 and later block Accessibility for apps installed from a downloaded APK. Open App info, tap the three-dot menu at the top right, choose \"Allow restricted settings\", confirm, then come back and turn AutoSkip on. Installing from Android Studio or with adb avoids this.

Also silences ads that have no Skip button. Sound comes back when the ad ends, or press a volume key.
Debug logging
Writes what AutoSkip sees to logcat (tag AutoSkip). Use it to fix AutoSkip after a YouTube update.

Not affiliated with YouTube or Google. Skippable ads only: AutoSkip presses the button YouTube already shows you. Ads without a Skip button still play (you can mute them).
